items.value: Two statements are correct — the Jhelum does pass through Wular Lake and Kanwar Lake is a meander-formed oxbow of the Gandak system; the Krishna does not directly feed Kolleru
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Wular, in the Kashmir Valley, is a floodplain lake of the Jhelum, which enters and leaves it. Statement 3 is correct in substance: Kanwar (Kabar) Taal in Begusarai is a residual oxbow lake left by the meandering of the Gandak system, though the river that actually formed it is the Burhi Gandak, so the stem is loose here. Statement 2 is wrong: Kolleru lies between the Krishna and Godavari deltas and is fed by the Budameru and Tammileru streams, not directly by the Krishna. Runner-up A, which follows if the Gandak/Burhi Gandak distinction is enforced strictly.

items.value: Two pairs are correct — Kamarajar Port (first corporatised major port) and Mundra (largest private port); Visakhapatnam is not India's largest container port
items.reasoning: Kamarajar (Ennore) Port is the only major port incorporated as a company under the Companies Act rather than run by a Port Trust, so pair 1 holds. Mundra, run by Adani, is India's largest privately owned port, so pair 2 holds. Pair 3 fails: India's largest container port is Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), which handles the bulk of national container traffic; Visakhapatnam is a large multi-cargo port but not the container leader.

items.value: Two are deciduous — mahua and teak; jackfruit is evergreen
items.reasoning: Teak (Tectona grandis) is the type species of India's tropical dry deciduous forests and sheds its leaves completely in the dry season. Mahua (Madhuca indica) is likewise deciduous, flowering on leafless branches between February and April, which is why its flowers are collected off the forest floor. Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is an evergreen tree that carries its dense leathery canopy through the year, so it does not count.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — India's arable area exceeds China's, but China irrigates a larger share of its cropland and has far higher yields
items.reasoning: India's arable area, roughly 155-160 million hectares, is the largest in the world and exceeds China's, which is nearer 120 million hectares, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: although the two countries have similar absolute irrigated areas, China's irrigated share of its much smaller cropland base is the higher proportion. Statement 3 is wrong: China's per-hectare yields in rice, wheat and most staples are substantially above India's, which is a standing point of comparison in Indian agricultural policy.

items.value: The Rann of Kutch
items.reasoning: The Rann of Kutch is a vast salt marsh occupying a former shallow arm of the Arabian Sea, left behind as the sea progressively withdrew through repeated falls in relative sea level combined with tectonic uplift and silting. It is the only option that is an extensive marshland. Bhitarkanika is a mangrove forest on an active delta, Marakkanam is a small worked salt pan, and the Naupada swamp is a limited coastal wetland, so none of them fits either the mechanism or the scale the question asks for.

items.value: Titanium
items.reasoning: Ilmenite is iron titanium oxide and rutile is titanium dioxide; both are the principal ores of titanium and the reason India's beach-sand mineral tracts in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha are commercially important. Iron is present in ilmenite only as the accompanying cation, not the mineral's economic value, so C is a distractor. Aluminium comes from bauxite and copper from sulphide ores, neither of which is related to these two minerals.

items.value: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
items.reasoning: The Democratic Republic of the Congo supplies roughly 70 per cent of world mined cobalt, chiefly as a by-product of copper mining in the Katanga copper belt, and this concentration is the central supply-chain risk discussed around electric-vehicle batteries. Argentina's strategic battery mineral is lithium, not cobalt; Botswana is a diamond producer; and Kazakhstan is significant for uranium.

items.value: Cameroon
items.reasoning: The Congo Basin spans the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo, the Central African Republic, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon, whose south-eastern rainforests drain into the Congo system. Nigeria lies in the Niger Basin, South Sudan in the Nile Basin, and Uganda drains to the Nile through Lake Victoria, so none of the other three belongs to the Congo Basin.

items.value: None of the three is correct
items.reasoning: Amarkantak is where the Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet in the Maikal hills, not the Sahyadri, which is the Western Ghats far to the south-west, so statement 1 fails. The Biligirirangan Hills lie in southern Karnataka and form a bridge between the Western and Eastern Ghats, having no connection with the Satpura range, so statement 2 fails. The Seshachalam Hills are in Andhra Pradesh and belong to the Eastern Ghats, not the southern end of the Western Ghats, so statement 3 fails.

items.value: None of the three is correct
items.reasoning: The East-West Corridor is part of the North-South and East-West Corridor project, which is separate from the Golden Quadrilateral, and it runs from Silchar to Porbandar, not Dibrugarh to Surat, so statement 1 is doubly wrong. The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway runs from Moreh to Mae Sot in Thailand, not Chiang Mai, so statement 2 is wrong. The BCIM Economic Corridor was conceived as a Kolkata-to-Kunming route through Dhaka and Mandalay, not from Varanasi, so statement 3 is wrong.

items.value: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect — power reactors do not need 60 per cent enrichment
items.reasoning: Statement-I is correct: coal supplies about seventy per cent of India's electricity while nuclear contributes only a few per cent, despite domestic uranium reserves. Statement-II is wrong: power reactors run on low-enriched uranium of roughly three to five per cent, and India's own pressurised heavy water reactors use natural uranium at 0.7 per cent because they are heavy-water moderated. Enrichment of sixty per cent and above is associated with weapons-relevant material, not routine electricity generation.

items.value: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect — marsupials are absent from India, but not because they need predator-free montane grassland
items.reasoning: Statement-I is correct: marsupials occur naturally only in Australasia and the Americas, and none is native to India. Statement-II is wrong on both counts: marsupials occupy deserts, rainforests, woodland and urban fringes rather than montane grassland alone, and they coexist with predators such as dingoes, quolls and raptors. Their absence from India is a matter of continental drift and biogeographic isolation, not habitat preference.

items.value: The International Union for Conservation of Nature
items.reasoning: The Invasive Species Specialist Group is one of the specialist groups of the IUCN Species Survival Commission, and it maintains the Global Invasive Species Database along with the list of 100 of the World's Worst Invasive Alien Species. UNEP and WWF work on invasive species but do not host this group, and the World Commission on Environment and Development was a one-off body that produced the Brundtland Report in 1987 and no longer exists.

items.value: Two are nocturnal or most active after sunset — the Malabar civet and the sambar; the lion-tailed macaque is diurnal
items.reasoning: The Malabar civet, like viverrids generally, is strictly nocturnal, which is one reason its survival status is so hard to confirm. The sambar is chiefly nocturnal and crepuscular, feeding and moving mainly from dusk onward. The lion-tailed macaque is diurnal, foraging in the rainforest canopy by day and sleeping at night, as all macaques do. The judgement call is the sambar, which some accounts describe as crepuscular rather than strictly nocturnal; reading it that way would give A.

items.value: Honeybees
items.reasoning: The waggle dance is the figure-of-eight movement performed by returning honeybee foragers on the vertical comb, in which the angle of the waggle run relative to gravity encodes the direction of the food source relative to the sun and the duration of the run encodes distance. It was decoded by Karl von Frisch. Butterflies and dragonflies are not eusocial and have no recruitment communication of this kind, and wasps do not use a dance language.

items.value: All four are correct — mushrooms include medicinal, psychoactive, insecticidal and bioluminescent species
items.reasoning: Each statement is hedged with 'some', and each is satisfied by known species: reishi and shiitake are used medicinally, Psilocybe species are psychoactive, several fungi produce insecticidal and nematicidal compounds used against insect pests, and genera such as Mycena, Omphalotus and Armillaria are bioluminescent, producing the glow known as foxfire. Nothing in the list requires the property to be general to all mushrooms, so all four hold.

items.value: Two are correct — Indian squirrels cache food in the ground and are omnivorous; they do not nest in ground burrows
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: the familiar Indian squirrels, the palm squirrels and the giant squirrels, are arboreal and build leaf-and-fibre nests or use tree hollows rather than digging burrows. Statement 2 is correct: they scatter-hoard nuts and seeds, burying them and recovering them later. Statement 3 is correct: besides fruit, nuts and bark they take insects, eggs and nestlings, which makes them omnivorous rather than purely granivorous. Runner-up A, if one declines to credit ground caching.

items.value: All three are correct — microbes grow above 100 degrees Celsius, below freezing, and below pH 3
items.reasoning: Hyperthermophilic archaea at deep-sea hydrothermal vents, such as Pyrolobus fumarii and Methanopyrus kandleri, grow above 100 degrees Celsius because the high pressure keeps water liquid. Psychrophiles multiply in polar brine channels at temperatures several degrees below zero, where dissolved salts prevent freezing. Acidophiles such as Picrophilus and Acidithiobacillus grow at pH values near or below 1, well under pH 3, in acid mine drainage and volcanic springs.

items.value: Orangutan
items.reasoning: Orangutans are great apes with documented stick-tool manufacture: they strip and shape twigs to probe tree holes for insects and to extract seeds from hard fruit, and the behaviour is transmitted culturally between populations. The fishing cat catches fish by paw and does not make tools, otters use stones as anvils but do not fashion sticks for insect extraction, and the sloth bear obtains termites by digging with its claws and sucking them up through its lips rather than by using an implement.

items.value: Three are established uses — aerosols, foam agents and fire-suppression agents; the lubricant use is not supportable
items.reasoning: Hydrofluorocarbons are documented as aerosol propellants, as blowing agents in the manufacture of insulating foam, and as clean-agent fire suppressants such as HFC-227ea, which replaced halons; those three are secure. Lubricants are the doubtful item: HFCs are refrigerants and are paired with polyol-ester lubricants in refrigeration circuits, but they are not themselves a lubricant ingredient, and the standard lists of HFC applications from ozone-regime sources do not include lubricant manufacture. This is a genuine two-way call between C and D, since a spray lubricant packaged with an HFC propellant could be read as HFCs being used in its making.

items.value: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct — the tax treatment is the reverse of what Statement-I claims, and InvITs are recognised as borrowers under SARFAESI
items.reasoning: Statement-I inverts the pass-through regime for business trusts: interest distributed by an InvIT is taxable in the unitholder's hands, while dividend distributed is exempt so long as the underlying special purpose vehicle has not opted for the concessional corporate rate. Statement-II is correct: InvITs and REITs were brought within the definition of borrower under the SARFAESI Act so that they could raise debt from banks and financial institutions against security. The judgement call is the exact scope of the dividend exemption, which is conditional rather than absolute, but the direction Statement-I asserts is wrong either way.

items.value: Both correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I — banks raised rates precisely because they believe monetary policy can restrain consumer prices
items.reasoning: Statement-I is a plain fact of 2022-23: the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of England and the Reserve Bank of India all raised policy rates after the pandemic. Statement-II states the working premise of inflation targeting, that tightening monetary conditions can pull demand and hence prices down. The two are causally linked, because the hikes were undertaken on exactly that assumption, so Statement-II is the explanation rather than a merely coincidental truth. Runner-up B, for a reader who treats the hikes as driven by the inflation itself rather than by the belief that policy can address it.

items.value: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect — carbon markets transfer resources between emitters, not from the private sector to the State
items.reasoning: Statement-I is defensible: emissions trading systems, the Clean Development Mechanism and now the Article 6 mechanisms of the Paris Agreement make carbon markets one of the most widely adopted mitigation instruments, and India has legislated for its own carbon credit trading scheme. Statement-II is wrong as a general description: in a cap-and-trade or offset market the payment flows from high-cost abaters to low-cost abaters and project developers, both usually private, which is precisely what distinguishes a market from a carbon tax, where the revenue does go to the State.

items.value: Conducting Open Market Operations
items.reasoning: Sterilisation means neutralising the effect on domestic money supply of the central bank's foreign exchange transactions: when the RBI buys dollars it releases rupees, and it withdraws that liquidity by selling government securities in open market operations, or through instruments such as the Market Stabilisation Scheme. The other three options describe distinct RBI functions, namely payment system oversight, debt and cash management as banker to government, and regulation of non-banking financial institutions, none of which has any liquidity-neutralising purpose.

items.value: Two are capital markets — the government bond market and the stock market; call money and treasury bills are money markets
items.reasoning: The capital market deals in instruments of more than one year's maturity, which covers the government bond or dated-securities market and the equity market. The call money market is overnight to fourteen-day borrowing between banks and is the shortest end of the money market. Treasury bills mature in 91, 182 or 364 days, all under a year, so they too are money market instruments. Maturity, not issuer, is the dividing line, which is why government paper appears on both sides.
